name: Ethal Anbuail
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ethal Anbuail was an Irish hero. He was the father of Caer, the romantic heroine beloved of Aonghus Óg, the god of the arts. He was a fairy king of Connacht. Koch recounts that Oengus longed for the woman he saw in his dream. Oengus waited a year for her. With the aid of Bodb Derg, he named her. The lovers met and flew to Brug na Bóinne as swans. Those who heard that swan sang slept not for three days and nights.

okr.objective: Rewrite the Ethal Anbuail entry with the full Caer narrative.
key_results: Describe him as the father of the heroine Caer
Note the fairy kingdom of Connacht
Cross the Koch dream and swan motif with the Brug na Bóinne
